findings_fixed: MAJOR: compare() silently de-duplicated duplicate ids, accepted dangling references, crashed with AttributeError on wrong-typed rows and never verified decision_digest - all could yield same on a malformed record
MAJOR: decode_trace walked the whole input uncharged, so max_work_units did not bound decode

MAJOR: max_input_bytes was bypassable - accounting sampled a subset of each row (form_type, both digests and the reference lists went uncharged), a 1.95x undercount that let a 35 KB input freeze complete under a 25 KB cap
MAJOR (test gap): decision_digest coverage of versions/scopes/candidates was unproven - two mutants deleting those payload fields still passed all 111 tests; now pinned per identity class
MAJOR->minor: _reference_list de-duplicated with a list scan, O(n^2) inside a nominally bounded call

MINOR: compare's index/sort/set-diff pre-passes ran uncharged; limits were validated on only some routes; decision_digest used .get() defaults and was row-order sensitive while compare is order-insensitive

MINOR: the AST import guard missed 'from parent import forbidden_child' and __import__(); NO_PARTICIPATING_COMPONENT did not block complete; the package docstring overstated what shape diagnostics catch

MINOR/NIT: handoff numbers, a regression sentence, a misleading test name, a tautological assertion, dead code, and the C-node fixture's scope identity (form_type was dropped, colliding 20 real scope ids and silently discarding 54 of 132 applies rows)
HARDENING: the compare diff now charges the real canonical encoding of each row too, closing the same byte-accounting class of hole on the manifest-vs-manifest route

RESIDUAL R1: the manifest validation pass (field checks, reference checks and the decision_digest re-derive) ran uncharged before the diff, and its reference check was quadratic. Now charged to the same budget with a set-based reference check - a 300k-row manifest compare with max_work_units=1 returns unavailable in 0.000s (was 4.321s).

RESIDUAL R2: the per-row byte envelope was charged once per REFERENCE, shrinking what fits inside the published max_input_bytes by roughly 20x for reference-heavy inputs (a 100 KB trace stopped fitting a 2 MiB cap). The envelope is now charged once per row and the row's canonical encoding carries the references - a 135 KB / 12000-reference trace freezes complete at 6.5% of the cap.
RESIDUAL R3: decision_digest silently skipped non-mapping rows, so garbage rows hashed the same as no rows. It now raises ValueError.
RESIDUAL R4: manifest scope rows were not type-checked beyond the id. regime/family/purpose must be non-empty strings and form_type null-or-string, matching the trace side.

FINAL OBSERVATION 1: compare byte-charged each row on three passes (validation, index, diff), so a domain that froze complete could still never compare same - a 456 KB trace froze complete yet compare returned unavailable. Rows are now byte-measured once, in the validation pass; the index and diff passes charge work only. Freeze and compare now agree: a 260 KB domain freezes complete and compares same.

FINAL OBSERVATION 2 (cosmetic): budget stops were worded 'while diffing' even when they happened during validation, and a stop inside the digest recompute surfaced as FROZEN_NOT_A_DECISION_MANIFEST. Both now report the budget reason.
findings_accepted_not_changed: RED-first ordering is evidenced by a receipt rather than by separate git commits, since tests and implementation landed in one commit; evidence/a_red.json records the original 51-failure run and the three post-RED assertion corrections

A fully-shaped forged winners-only trace that omits participants and still asserts inventory_complete=true is not detectable from inside the input. This is the card's uncertifiable external omission; documented in the package docstring, findings.md and handoff.json known_gaps rather than papered over
